A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LayerDAG study. Their text, equations, five tables, four figures and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original DAG-generation experiments, conditional-generation and generalization evaluations, and an extended synthetic-data experiment in Appendix D (Tables 1 and 3–5).

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main evaluations and Appendix D's attribute-validity experiment.

M1.justification: The core generation, training and diffusion procedures remain the same. However, v2 removes the description of sinusoidal layer-depth positional encodings from Section 3.2 without stating whether this component was removed from the model or only from the exposition.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LP, its three-attribute variant, TPU Tile, HLS and NA-Edge, including the same interpolation and extrapolation scenarios. The new discussion of trees is an applicability caveat, not an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 3 and 4 retain D-VAE, GraphRNN, GraphPNAS, OneShotDAG and LayerDAG (T = 1). Appendix D retains its D-VAE and GraphRNN comparisons, and Figure 2 retains the same comparators.

E3.justification: The reported splits, HLS subsampling, held-out label quantiles, metrics and surrogate-model selection procedures are unchanged (Section 5 and Appendices C–F). Removing the preprocessing citation does not establish a changed preprocessing procedure.

E4.justification: v2 removes Section 3.2's brief qualitative assessment of performance under different positional encodings. The non-autoregressive and single-step ablations, denoising-schedule comparison and Appendix D attribute-validity analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 1, 3 and 4 retain the same ± reporting. Appendix D still states that Table 5 results are averaged over three random seeds; no uncertainty-estimation or repeated-run reporting changes are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 removes the qualitative findings that one-hot layer encodings may hurt performance and sinusoidal encodings improve generation quality in many cases. Numerical results in Tables 1 and 3–5 and the plotted results are unchanged; Table 2's HLS layer count changes from 27.8 to 27.75, which is equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1 is retained, but its justification drops the explicit assertion that layer-depth positional encodings are permutation equivariant. The remaining invariance argument, DAG factorization and Appendix A diffusion derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: layerwise autoregressive diffusion for DAG generation, modeling directional and logical dependencies, and improved generation and generalization for system benchmarking.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 newly explains that the linear denoising schedule may be unhelpful for trees with stationary layer distributions. Section 5.3 acknowledges the limited practical strength of the extrapolation results. The positional-encoding tradeoff discussion is removed.

D1.justification: v2 removes the explicit sinusoidal layer-index encoding specification and the statement identifying Wang et al. (2024) as the preprocessing source. Appendix implementation details, hardware and software information, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kahn (1962) and Tarjan (1972) for topological ordering, removes the positional-encoding and length-generalization references, and removes Wang et al. (2024). The central positioning against existing DAG and undirected-graph generators is retained.

P1.justification: There are localized wording changes, a deleted positional-encoding discussion, short explanatory additions and an updated ICLR 2025 publication header. The overall section hierarchy and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained. Figure 2 moves from page 11 to page 10, and Figure 4 moves from page 17 to page 16; surrounding text and table spacing reflow. The figure graphics and table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new schedule limitation and qualification of the extrapolation results improve interpretive calibration. However, removing the layer-depth encoding specification and preprocessing attribution reduces reproducibility clarity, without explaining whether the implementation changed. With the quantitative evidence unchanged, these competing effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
